_comment: The install commands of the landing page (site/index.html) and the one place they are written. scripts/site/build.py --check fails unless README.md and docs/user/src/how-to/install.md show every `cmd` exactly as written here. Text in `note` may use `backticks` and [links](url).

tabs.label: Linux & macOS
tabs.note: No sudo. The script checks every file against the release's `SHA256SUMS`. On Linux it installs the AppImage as `~/.local/bin/nauvi-desktop` with a menu entry; on macOS `nauvi.app` into Applications. Because curl sets no quarantine flag, macOS opens the app without the "could not verify" prompt. Run it again to upgrade.

tabs.label: Debian & Ubuntu

steps.title: Add the signed apt repository and install

tabs.note: The script refuses the repository key unless its fingerprint is `B2B644E79A85C438FC3EB8C5408A65C769395FBF`. After that, `sudo apt upgrade` keeps nauvi up to date. The package is the desktop app (x86_64); for the CLI use the Linux & macOS script with `--cli`.

tabs.label: Homebrew
tabs.note: If Homebrew refuses the tap, run `brew trust nexburst/tap` first. The app is not signed yet: the first launch says "Apple could not verify…". Click Done, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Open Anyway**.

tabs.label: Windows
tabs.note: The app comes from the `.msi` and updates itself; the CLI goes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nauvi\bin`. The builds are not signed yet, so SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC": click More info, then Run anyway.
